name: Zeus
summary: Father of gods and men. Zeus favours neither army for its own sake: he keeps his promise to Thetis to honour Achilles, and he weighs the fates of heroes on golden scales.

moments.text: Nods to Thetis's request to let the Trojans win until Achilles is honoured.
Forbids the other gods from joining the battle.
Grieves but lets his own son Sarpedon die.
Lifts his golden scales; Hector's doom sinks.

fate: Above the sides — he lets the gods take part in the fighting from Book 20.
fact: In Book 14 Hera lulls him to sleep so Poseidon can help the Greeks behind his back.

name: Hera
summary: Wife of Zeus and a relentless enemy of Troy. She schemes constantly to help the Greeks, even against her husband's orders.

moments.text: Sends Athena to stop Achilles drawing his sword on Agamemnon.
Borrows Aphrodite's charmed band to distract Zeus.
Strikes Artemis with her own bow during the battle of the gods.

fact: Book 24 hints at the Judgment of Paris — the insult behind her hatred of Troy.

name: Athena
role: Goddess of wisdom and war strategy
summary: Daughter of Zeus and the Greeks' most active divine ally. She guides heroes, deflects spears and, at the end, tricks Hector.

moments.text: Holds Achilles back by his hair as he reaches for his sword.
Disguised as Laodocus, persuades Pandarus to break the truce.
Rides with Diomedes as he wounds Ares.
Takes the form of Deiphobus so Hector stands and fights.

fact: Only Achilles can see her when she stops him in Book 1.

name: Apollo
role: God of archery, healing and plague
summary: Son of Zeus and Leto, and Troy's strongest divine protector. His arrows open the poem with a plague.

moments.text: Sends nine days of plague after Agamemnon insults his priest Chryses.
Strikes Patroclus from behind and knocks off his armour.
Protects Hector's body from harm while Achilles abuses it.

fate: Sides with Troy. Hector, dying, says Apollo will help Paris kill Achilles.
fact: In Book 21 he refuses to duel his uncle Poseidon, saying mortals are not worth gods fighting over.

image.title: Apollo pouring a libation, white-ground cup (detail)

name: Poseidon
role: God of the sea and earthquakes
summary: Brother of Zeus. Poseidon helps the Greeks, partly out of an old grudge against Troy's former king Laomedon.

moments.text: Rallies the Greeks while Zeus looks away.
Saves the Trojan Aeneas — fate says he must survive.
Reminds Apollo that Laomedon cheated them both.

fact: He says he built Troy's walls for Laomedon, who then refused to pay.

name: Aphrodite
summary: Paris's patron and the mother of the Trojan hero Aeneas. She protects her favourites but is no fighter.

moments.text: Snatches Paris away from his duel with Menelaus.
Wounded on the hand by Diomedes while rescuing Aeneas.

fact: After Diomedes wounds her she flees to Olympus, where Zeus tells her to stick to love, not war.

image.title: Aphrodite riding a goose, white-ground cup (detail)

name: Ares
summary: Violent and reckless, Ares fights for Troy — and gets the worst of it whenever he meets Athena.

moments.text: Wounded by Diomedes, whose spear Athena drives home.
Knocked down by a boulder thrown by Athena.

fact: When wounded he bellows as loudly as nine or ten thousand men in battle.

name: Hephaestus
role: God of fire and the forge
summary: The lame smith of the gods. He makes Achilles the most famous armour in literature.

moments.text: Calms a quarrel between Zeus and Hera on Olympus.
Forges new armour and a great shield for Achilles.
Turns his fire on the river god who is drowning Achilles.

fact: The shield he makes shows a whole world: cities at peace and war, farms, vineyards and dancing.

image.title: Apollo in the Forge of Vulcan (detail)

name: Hermes
summary: Listed with the Greek-side gods in Book 20, but his great moment is an act of mercy: guiding Priam to Achilles.

moments.text: Politely refuses to fight Leto.
Sent by Zeus, disguised as a young Myrmidon, he leads Priam safely through the Greek camp.

fate: Sides with the Greeks, yet serves Zeus's will in helping Priam.
fact: He casts sleep on the Greek sentries so Priam's wagon can pass unseen.

name: Artemis
summary: Apollo's twin sister. She supports Troy but comes off badly in the battle of the gods.

moments.text: Scolds Apollo for not fighting Poseidon.
Hera boxes her ears with her own bow, and she flees in tears.

fact: She and Apollo are children of Leto, who also sides with Troy.

name: Thetis
summary: A goddess of the sea married to a mortal. She knows her son's life will be short and does everything she can for him.

moments.text: Clasps Zeus's knees and asks him to honour Achilles.
Asks Hephaestus to forge new armour for her son.
Tells Achilles that Zeus wants him to return Hector's body.

fact: She is not an Olympian but a Nereid — one of the daughters of the old sea god.
